projects.name: 潍坊十笏园
projects.name_en: The Shihu Garden in Weifang
projects.level: 全国重点文物保护单位（1988年第三批）
projects.address: 潍坊市潍城区胡家牌坊街345号
projects.content_zh: 十笏园位于潍坊市潍城区胡家牌坊街，又名丁家花园，原为明清缙绅故宅，明嘉靖年间为刑部郎中胡邦佐的宅第，清顺治年间归彰德知府陈兆鸾，道光年间归直隶布政使郭熊飞，光绪十一年（1885年）被潍县首富丁善宝以重金购得，修葺北部三间旧楼题名砚香楼，开挖水池，堆叠假山，始成花园，1988年被国务院公布为第三批全国重点文物保护单位。「笏」是古代大臣上朝时手持的狭长手板，多用玉、象牙或竹片制成。丁善宝在《十笏园记》中解释命名之意：以其小而易就也，署其名曰十笏园，亦以其小而名之也。「十笏」一词出自唐代《法苑珠林》，其中记载印度吠舍哩国有维摩居士故宅基，唐显庆年间王玄策出使西域经过此地，以笏量宅基，只有十笏，故号方丈之室；后人即以「十笏」形容面积狭小的建筑。十笏园现存园址南北深七十米，东西宽四十四米，占地三千四百平方米，平面呈长方形，由中、西、东三条古建筑轴线组成，各布庭院三、四进不等。中轴线是园林的中心，院内前部以水池为中心，四周配置四合式庭院，水池东岸堆叠半壁假山，山顶山脚配置蔚秀亭、落霞亭、漪岚亭和稳如舟等亭舍；水池西岸经矩形游廊南通西跨院，北达春雨楼与砚香楼庭院；池岸以太湖石堆砌自然驳岸，将半壁山与游廊呈弧状连接。池中小岛之上建四照亭，取四面阳光普照之意，方形六檩卷棚式歇山顶，四周设坐凳栏杆，亭中有清代状元曹鸿勋所题「四照亭」横匾，亭外悬清代书法家桂馥手书的「涛音」二字，亭柱对联为「清风明月本无价，近水远山皆有情」，亭前悬对联「望云惭高鸟，临水愧游鱼」，亭内设石桌石凳，是当年园主举觞流连、咏诗之处。东路主体建筑碧云斋原为丁氏居室，西路主体建筑诵芬书屋、深柳读书堂、秋声馆与静如山房等为丁氏私塾与客房。园内共建亭台楼榭二十四处、房舍六十七间，其中山顶落霞亭为1949年以后增建。十笏园最令人称道的是其在极小空间中营造极丰富景境的能力。为突出砚香楼前的空间效果，园中对假山上下的四照亭、稳如舟、蓬莱三仙岛、蔚秀亭、漪岚亭、小沧浪亭等建筑景点，均采取小尺度构筑；在造景处理上，池东以摹拟自然景观为主、建筑为辅，池西则以建筑实景为主、仿自然驳岸叠石为辅，虚实呼应，富而不俗，是一处兼具江南与江北园林风格的私家小园优秀实例，被称为中国古典造园艺术中的奇葩，也是北方园林「袖珍化」的杰出代表。十笏园还与潍坊深厚的手工艺传统紧密相连：潍坊核雕艺人能在四厘米长的桃核上完整刻出十笏园的长廊、假山、四照亭、春雨楼与砚香楼，景物布局完全依照实景定位，刻画惟妙惟肖，被誉为鬼工神技。
projects.content_en: The Shihu Garden, also called the Ding Family Garden, stands on Hujia Paifang Street in Weicheng District, Weifang.Originally the residence of Ming and Qing gentry, it belonged in the Jiajing reign of the Ming to Hu Bangzuo, a director in the Ministry of Justice, then in the Shunzhi reign to Chen Zhaoluan, prefect of Zhangde, and in the Daoguang reign to Guo Xiongfei, administration commissioner of Zhili; in 1885 Ding Shanbao, the richest man in Weixian, bought it for a large sum, restored the three old northern bays as the Inkstone Fragrance Tower, excavated a pool and piled a rockery, thus creating the garden.In 1988 it was listed by the State Council as a National Key Cultural Heritage Site in the third batch.A hu is the narrow tablet held by ministers at audience, usually of jade, ivory or bamboo. Ding Shanbao explained the name in his Record of the Shihu Garden: because it was small and easily accomplished, I named it the Garden of Ten Tablets, naming it for its smallness.The term ten tablets comes from the Tang work Forest of Pearls in the Garden of the Dharma, which records that in the Indian state of Vaishali there was the foundation of the house of the layman Vimalakirti; when Wang Xuance passed that way on an embassy to the western regions in the Xianqing era he measured the foundation with his tablet and found it only ten tablets wide, whence the name abbot's chamber; later generations used ten tablets to describe a building of very small area.The surviving garden is seventy metres deep from north to south and forty-four metres wide from east to west, covering 3,400 square metres on a rectangular plan, composed of three building axes - central, western and eastern - each with three or four successive courtyards.The central axis is the heart of the garden; its front part centres on the pool with four-building courtyards around it, a half-wall rockery piled on the east bank with the Weixiu, Luoxia, Yilan and Wenruzhou pavilions set at its top and foot; on the west bank a rectangular covered walk leads south to the western cross court and north to the Spring Rain Tower and Inkstone Fragrance Tower courts.The pool edge is built of Taihu rock as a natural bank, linking the half-wall mountain and the covered walk in an arc.On an island in the pool stands the Four-Sided Light Pavilion, named because sunlight falls on all four sides; square, of six purlins with a round-ridge hip-gable roof and bench rails around, it holds a horizontal plaque inscribed by Cao Hongxun, a Qing optimus, and outside hangs the characters Wave Sound in the hand of the Qing calligrapher Gui Fu.Its columns carry the couplet the clear breeze and bright moon are priceless, the near water and distant hills all have feeling, and in front hangs the couplet I am shamed before the high-flying birds when I watch the clouds, and before the swimming fish when I face the water.Stone tables and stools inside are where the owner once raised his cup and composed verse.The principal building of the eastern axis, the Biyun Studio, was the Ding family's living quarters; the principal buildings of the western axis - the Songfen Study, the Deep Willow Reading Hall, the Autumn Sound Lodge and the Jingru Mountain Lodge - served as the family school and guest rooms.In all the garden has twenty-four pavilions, terraces, towers and waterside halls and sixty-seven rooms, of which the Luoxia Pavilion on the hill was added after 1949.What is most admired about the Shihu Garden is its ability to create extremely rich scenery in an extremely small space.To strengthen the space in front of the Inkstone Fragrance Tower, all the structures above and below the rockery - the Four-Sided Light Pavilion, the Wenruzhou, the three isles of Penglai, the Weixiu Pavilion, the Yilan Pavilion and the Xiaocanglang Pavilion - are built at reduced scale.In composition, the east of the pool is dominated by simulated natural scenery with buildings subordinate, while the west is dominated by built scenery with the imitated natural bank and rockwork subordinate; the two answer each other in void and solid, rich yet never vulgar.It is an outstanding example of a small private garden combining the styles of south and north, celebrated as a marvel of Chinese classical garden art and as a masterly instance of the miniaturisation of the northern garden.The garden is also closely tied to Weifang's deep craft tradition: Weifang peach-stone carvers can render the whole garden - corridors, rockery, Four-Sided Light Pavilion, Spring Rain Tower and Inkstone Fragrance Tower - on a peach stone four centimetres long, laid out exactly as in reality and marvellously lifelike, a feat praised as divine craftsmanship.
highlights: 1988年列入第三批全国重点文物保护单位
清光绪十一年丁善宝购得改建，又名丁家花园
十笏出自《法苑珠林》维摩居士方丈之室典故
占地三千四百平方米，南北七十米、东西四十四米
中东西三轴，二十四处亭台楼榭、六十七间房舍
四照亭居池中，六檩卷棚歇山顶，曹鸿勋题匾
池东摹拟自然、池西建筑实景，虚实呼应
核雕艺人能在四厘米桃核上刻出全园

projects.name: 邹城孟府与孟庙
projects.name_en: The Mencius Mansion and Mencius Temple in Zoucheng
projects.dynasty: 北宋景祐四年（1037）始建，现存为明清格局
projects.level: 全国重点文物保护单位（1988年第三批）
projects.address: 济宁市邹城市亚圣府街44号
projects.content_zh: 孟庙、孟府与孟林合称「三孟」，位于济宁邹城市，分别是孟子的祠庙、孟子嫡系后裔的住所与孟子及其后裔的墓地。孟庙又称亚圣庙，始建于北宋景祐四年（1037年），由孔子四十五代孙孔道辅建于孟子墓旁，元丰年间因地处偏远、瞻祭不便而迁建至邹城东关，宣和三年（1121年）又因濒水易坏而迁至今址，此后历经金、元、明、清多次重修扩建，至清康熙五十四年（1715年）形成现存规模。1988年，孟庙及孟府被国务院公布为第三批全国重点文物保护单位；2006年，孟林被公布为第六批全国重点文物保护单位并与之合并，更名为孟庙、孟府和孟林。孟庙呈长方形，共五进院落，殿宇六十四楹、木坊三座、石坊一座，占地两万四千平方米，是山东省现存历史最久远、保存最完整的古建筑群之一，其规模仅次于曲阜孔庙。孟庙的布局为：前三进为导引式庭院，后二进分为左、中、右三路。中轴线上自南至北依次为棂星门、亚圣庙坊、仪门、承圣门、亚圣殿、寝殿；中路的主体建筑亚圣殿是孟庙的核心，殿高十七米，进深二十点四八米，横宽二十七点七米，为宫殿式建筑，四周有石柱二十六根，殿前廊檐下的八根石柱饰以浅浮雕，门侧四柱正面刻翼龙在云中翱翔，其余各面刻宝相牡丹或西番莲花，大殿正面高悬「亚圣殿」楷书贴金匾额，殿正中门额上挂「道阐尼山」横匾，殿内迎面抱柱对联为「尊王言必称尧舜，忧世心同切禹颜」，匾额与对联均为清乾隆帝手书；殿内上方横悬清雍正帝手书「守先待后」金匾；殿内正中神龛内供奉衮冕九旒九章的孟子塑像，东侧神龛内供奉孟子弟子乐正子塑像。东路为启贤门，有启圣殿、启圣寝殿；西路为致敬门，有致严堂、祧祖祠、焚帛池。孟府又称亚圣府，位于孟庙西侧，是孟子嫡系后裔世代居住之处，始建于北宋末期，距今已有八百余年历史，南北长二百二十六米，东西宽九十九米，占地两万两千四百平方米，共七进院落，楼堂亭阁一百六十余间，前为衙署，中为内宅，后为花园，是一座典型的中国封建贵族府第。中轴线上自南至北依次为大门、二门、仪门、大堂、世恩堂、赐书楼、缘绿楼。大堂为孟府主体建筑，建于台基之上，面阔五间，硬山顶，檐下正中悬清雍正帝御书「七篇贻矩」匾额，堂前有月台，置日晷、嘉量，两侧设有鼓乐楼。孟庙孟府存有大量碑刻，以及历代封建帝王赐予的制服、题字、龙袍、圣旨，还有家族档案、印书木板、古籍字画等珍贵文物，为研究中国古代贵族生活、礼制建筑与家族制度提供了极为重要的实物资料。与曲阜孔庙孔府相比，孟庙孟府规模略小，但建筑的时代跨度更为完整，保留了宋、元、明、清各个时期的建筑做法，在建筑史上具有不可替代的断代标尺价值。
projects.content_en: The Mencius Temple, Mansion and Grove, known as the Three Meng, lie in Zoucheng, Jining, and are respectively the temple of Mencius, the residence of his direct descendants, and the cemetery of Mencius and his heirs.The Mencius Temple, also called the Temple of the Second Sage, was first built in 1037 by Kong Daofu, a descendant of Confucius in the forty-fifth generation, beside the tomb of Mencius; it was moved to the eastern suburb of Zoucheng in the Yuanfeng era because the site wasremote and inconvenient for worship, and again in 1121 because the site was prone to water damage, after which it was repeatedly rebuilt and extended under the Jin, Yuan, Ming and Qing, reaching its present scale in 1715.In 1988 the temple and mansion were listed by the State Council as National Key Cultural Heritage Sites in the third batch; in 2006 the Mencius Grove was added in the sixth batch and merged with them under the joint name.The temple is rectangular, with five successive courtyards, sixty-four bays of halls, three wooden archways and one stone archway, covering twenty-four thousand square metres; it is among the oldest and best-preserved ancient building complexes in Shandong, second in scale only to the Confucius Temple in Qufu.Its disposition is three introductory courts followed by two courts divided into left, central and right routes.On the central axis from south to north stand the Lattice Star Gate, the Temple of the Second Sage archway, the ceremonial gate, the Sacred-Inheriting Gate, the Hall of the Second Sage and the Rear Hall.The Hall of the Second Sage is the core: seventeen metres high, 20.48 metres deep and 27.7 metres wide, built in palace style with twenty-six stone columns, of which the eight under the front eaves carry shallow relief, while the four flanking the doors show winged dragons soaring in clouds and the rest show medallion peonies or passion flowers.A gilded plaque in regular script reading Hall of the Second Sage hangs on the front, and a horizontal tablet, The Way Elucidated at Mount Ni, above the central doorway; the couplet inside reads, in honouring the king his words always invoke Yao and Shun, in grieving for the age his heart is one with Yu and Yan - all in the hand of the Qianlong emperor.A gilded horizontal plaque in the hand of the Yongzheng emperor, Guarding the Forebears and Awaiting Those to Come, hangs above; the central niche enshrines a statue of Mencius in a robe and crown with nine pendants and nine emblems, and the eastern niche a statue of his disciple Yuezhengzi.The eastern route, through the Qixian Gate, holds the Hall of the Enlightened Sage and its rear hall; the western route, through the Zhijing Gate, holds the Zhiyan Hall, the Ancestor Temple and the Silk-Burning Pool.The Mansion, or Mansion of the Second Sage, lies west of the temple and was the residence of Mencius's direct descendants through the generations; first built in the late Northern Song, it is more than eight hundred years old, 226 metres from north to south and 99 metres from east to west, covering 22,400 square metres with seven successive courtyards and more than one hundred and sixty rooms of towers, halls, pavilions and chambers.It has offices at the front, inner quarters in the middle and a garden at the rear - a classic Chinese feudal aristocratic mansion.On the central axis from south to north stand the main gate, second gate, ceremonial gate, great hall, the Hall of Inherited Grace, the Bestowed-Books Tower and the Green-Edge Tower.The great hall, the principal building, stands on a platform, five bays wide with a gable roof, carrying at the centre of its eaves the plaque Seven Chapters Bequeath the Rule in the hand of the Yongzheng emperor; before it is a moon terrace with a sundial and standard measures, flanked by drum and music towers.The temple and mansion preserve a wealth of steles and precious objects - court robes, inscriptions, dragon robes and imperial edicts bestowed by emperors, together with family archives, printing blocks and rare books and paintings - providing exceptionally important material for the study of Chinese aristocratic life, ritual architecture and the family system.Compared with the Confucius Temple and Mansion at Qufu, the Meng complex is somewhat smaller, but its buildings span a more complete range of periods, preserving construction practice from the Song, Yuan, Ming and Qing and thus serving as an irreplaceable chronological yardstick in architectural history.

projects.name: 青州偶园
projects.name_en: The Ou Garden in Qingzhou
projects.dynasty: 明代衡王府东花园，清康熙年间改建
projects.address: 潍坊市青州市偶园街197号，青州古城内
projects.content_zh: 偶园位于青州古城偶园街，当地称「冯家花园」，是清康熙年间文华殿大学士兼刑部尚书冯溥的私家花园，也是中国北方现存为数不多的「康熙风格」园林建筑。明宪宗成化二十三年（1487年），皇帝朱见深封其第七子朱祐楎为衡王，弘治十二年（1499年）就藩青州，在建造富丽堂皇的衡王府的同时，于东华门外建造了一座花园，名东花园；按照明王朝的规定，东花园的布局与规模都与皇宫内的御花园相仿，只是规模略小。约一百八十余年后，清文华殿大学士、太子太傅冯溥在告老还乡之前，将他在北京的万柳堂献给皇上，皇上把原衡王府的东花园赐给了他；冯溥将东花园整修改建，取「无独有偶」之意，命名为「偶园」。偶园北面与古朴宽大的冯氏宗祠、楼台参差的冯宅连为一体，互相衬托，实际上是一组宅第、宗祠、园林相结合的三位一体的古代建筑群体，至今已有五百多年的历史；现在宗祠与宅第大部分已毁，花园仍保持完好。走进园门，一条砖石甬道向东延伸，路旁竹影摇曳，四株明朝的大桂花左右对称排列——据记载这些桂花是明朝衡王府的遗物，至今已经历四百多年，仍然枝繁叶茂；旁边有朝北的小门，上书「偶园门」，透过小园门与墙上的漏窗往里看，只见亭台错落、山多林茂，如同国画一般。园中坐北朝南的古建筑称「佳山堂」，是冯溥待客与写作的场所，冯溥在偶园内生活了十年，写下许多优美的诗篇，所著《佳山堂集》即是以佳山堂命名的。堂前沿东、南两墙成半月形环列的假山，就是著名的三峰假山，这是偶园最富吸引力的所在。假山在结构上分为坪、峰、涧、台四部分，每部分体现各自的主题，特色分明，使整个假山繁而不乱、静中有变、层次分明、境界高雅，于一园之内显出千里之势，被誉为「国宝」。据园林专家考证，青州偶园假山是明末清初著名叠石家张南垣之子张然的作品，其艺术构思与叠石风格技巧与中南海瀛台完全一致，是中国唯一幸存的「康熙风格」的园林假山。园内还有明代遗存的三株迎春花，虽老态龙钟，但每年隆冬都会绽开满枝黄花；园中的福、寿、康、宁四大奇石弥足珍贵，当时就有「一两石头一两银」之说；此外还有莲池、凝碧池、松风阁、卧云亭、望春楼、大方池等景观，小桥流水、古柏参天，充分体现了中国造园艺术的高超成就。
projects.content_en: The Ou Garden, locally called the Feng Family Garden, stands on Ou Garden Street in the old city of Qingzhou; it was the private garden of Feng Pu, Grand Secretary of the Wenhua Hall and Minister of Justice under the Kangxi emperor, and is one of the few surviving Kangxi-style gardens in northern China.In 1487 the Chenghua emperor enfeoffed his seventh son Zhu Youhui as Prince of Heng, who took up his fief at Qingzhou in 1499; while building a splendid princely palace he also laid out a garden outside the eastern Hua gate, called the Eastern Garden, which by Ming regulation matched the imperial garden in layout and scale, only slightly smaller.Some one hundred and eighty years later Feng Pu, shortly before retiring from office, presented his Willow Garden in Beijing to the emperor, who in turn granted him the former Eastern Garden of the Heng palace; Feng Pu restored and remodelled it and named it the Ou Garden, taking the sense of not being alone, that there is a counterpart to everything.To the north the garden joined the spacious Feng ancestral hall and the Feng residence with its tiers of terraces, the whole forming a three-in-one complex of dwelling, ancestral temple and garden more than five hundred years old; the hall and residence have largely been destroyed, but the garden survives intact.Entering, a brick and stone path runs east, bamboos swaying beside it, with four great Ming osmanthus trees set symmetrically to left and right - by tradition survivors of the Ming princely palace, still flourishing after more than four hundred years.Beside them a small north-facing gate bears the inscription Ou Garden Gate, and through it and the pierced windows in the wall one sees pavilions scattered among dense planting, like a Chinese painting.The ancient building facing south in the garden is the Jiashan, or Fine Mountain, Hall, where Feng Pu received guests and wrote; he lived in the garden for ten years and composed many fine poems, and his collected works, the Jiashan Tang Ji, is named after it.Along the eastern and southern walls in front of the hall, arranged in a half-moon, lies the famous three-peak rockery, the greatest attraction of the garden.Structurally the rockery is in four parts - terrace, peak, ravine and platform - each with its own theme and distinct character, so that the whole is rich without confusion, varied within stillness, clearly layered and of lofty conception, suggesting a thousand li of landscape within a single garden; it is honoured as a national treasure.Specialists have established that the rockery is the work of Zhang Ran, son of the celebrated late Ming and early Qing rockery master Zhang Nanyuan; its conception and its technique of stone piling correspond exactly to those of Yingtai in the Zhongnanhai, and it is the only surviving Kangxi-style garden rockery in China.The garden also preserves three Ming winter jasmines which, old as they are, burst into yellow blossom every deep winter; the four rare stones named Fortune, Longevity, Health and Peace are treasures of which it was said that one ounce of stone was worth one ounce of silver.Other features include the Lotus Pond, the Azure-Congealing Pool, the Pine Wind Pavilion, the Cloud-Resting Pavilion, the Spring-Viewing Tower and the Great Square Pool, with little bridges, running water and towering ancient cypresses, fully demonstrating the achievement of Chinese garden art.

projects.name: 桓台王渔洋故居与四世宫保坊
projects.name_en: The Wang Yuyang Residence and the Four Generations Palace Guard Arch in Huantai
projects.level: 全国重点文物保护单位（四世宫保坊）/ 山东省文物保护单位（忠勤祠、王渔洋故居）
projects.address: 淄博市桓台县新城镇，桓台古县城内
projects.content_zh: 桓台新城镇是山东省唯一的中国历史文化名镇，自金正大五年（1228年）作为治所建县，至今已有近八百年历史，镇域内留存有古建筑、古遗址、古墓葬等各级文物保护单位二十余处，其中省级文物保护单位五处，四世宫保砖牌坊为全国重点文物保护单位。新城王氏家族是明清时期著名的科举世家与仕宦望族，有进士三十名、举人五十二名、贡生一百五十八名，堪称「齐鲁第一进士家族」，素有「江北青箱」之誉。王渔洋（王士禛）是新城王氏最杰出的代表，官至刑部尚书，是清代著名的文学家、诗论家，创立「神韵说」，被尊为「一代诗宗」。王渔洋故里景区包括忠勤祠、王渔洋故居与四世宫保坊三处主要文物。忠勤祠又称王家祠堂，是一组典型的明代建筑，始建于明万历十六年（1588年），现存建筑建于万历三十年（1602年），为纪念王渔洋高祖王重光平蛮功成、督木殉职而敕建，因嘉靖皇帝手书「忠勤可悯」而得名，距今已有四百余年历史，占地一万多平方米，是山东省重点文物保护单位、山东省爱国主义教育基地。忠勤祠内碑碣林立，有「齐鲁小碑林」之称，石刻分为原文镌刻与集字石刻两类：原文镌刻由当时的著名书法家亲笔所书，如邢侗的《王氏大槐记》、董其昌的《草诀歌》、祝允明的《春荫诗》等，堪称石刻艺术瑰宝；集字石刻则从钟繇、王羲之、王献之、欧阳询、虞世南、褚遂良、颜真卿、柳公权等名家墨宝中以文选字、集字而成，然后摩勒上石，再请江南高手精工刻成，其撰文、书法、镌刻并称「三绝」，名闻海内。王渔洋故居建于清康熙二十四年（1685年），是王渔洋在其曾祖王之垣所建长春园故址上增葺的西城别墅，现占地一万五千平方米，建筑面积七千多平方米，保留明、清、民国时期建筑一百零八间，主体建筑为五进院落，规模庞大，雕梁画栋、曲径通幽、茂林修竹、古朴典雅，突出体现了融官宦宅邸、古代民居、祠堂建筑、小型园林为一体的独特建筑风格，现为山东省重点文物保护单位。四世宫保坊始建于明万历四十七年（1619年），为表彰王渔洋伯祖、兵部尚书王象乾五戍边关、护国有功而特许建造，朝廷追赠其祖上三代均为「光禄大夫柱国太子太保兵部尚书」，因此称为「四世宫保」。牌坊坐北朝南、跨街而立，高十五米，面宽九点二米，形式为中间高、两边低的宫殿式样，坊额「四世宫保」四个大字字体工整、笔力遒劲。四世宫保坊是新城七十二座牌坊中唯一保存完整的一座，整组建筑除基座外全为砖雕结构，融人文、建筑、雕塑、书法、绘画于一体，造型别致、气势雄伟、工艺精妙，以古朴典雅闻名遐迩，被誉为「华夏第一砖坊」。
projects.content_en: Xincheng Town in Huantai is the only town in Shandong designated a China Historical and Cultural Town; it became the seat of county government in 1228 and is nearly eight hundred years old, preserving more than twenty protected sites - ancient buildings, sites and tombs - of which five are protected at province level and the Four Generations Palace Guard brick archway at national level.The Wang family of Xincheng was a celebrated examination and official dynasty of the Ming and Qing, producing thirty metropolitan graduates, fifty-two provincial graduates and one hundred and fifty-eight tribute students - the foremost family of metropolitan graduates in Shandong, known as the Blue Casket of the North.Wang Yuyang, or Wang Shizhen, was its most distinguished member: he rose to Minister of Justice and became a famous Qing man of letters and poetic theorist, founder of the doctrine of spiritual resonance and honoured as the poet-laureate of his age.The Wang Yuyang heritage area comprises three principal monuments: the Zhongqin Ancestral Hall, the Wang Yuyang Residence and the Four Generations Palace Guard Arch.The Zhongqin Hall, or Wang family shrine, is a typical Ming building complex, first erected in 1588 in the Wanli reign, the surviving structures dating from 1602; it was built by imperial decree to commemorate Wang Chongguang, Wang Yuyang's great-great-grandfather, who pacified the southern tribes and died supervising timber procurement, and it takes its name from the Jiajing emperor's own inscription, loyal and diligent, deserving compassion.Now more than four hundred years old and covering over ten thousand square metres, it is a key provincial protected site and a provincial patriotic education base.Steles crowd the hall, earning it the name Little Forest of Steles of Shandong, in two classes: original inscriptions written by celebrated calligraphers of the day - Xing Tong's Record of the Wang Family's Great Locust Tree, Dong Qichang's Song of the Cursive Formula, Zhu Yunming's Poem of Spring Shade and others - which are treasures of the carver's art; and composite inscriptions, in which characters were selected from the works of Zhong Yao, Wang Xizhi, Wang Xianzhi, Ouyang Xun, Yu Shinan, Chu Suiliang, Yan Zhenqing and Liu Gongquan, assembled into texts, transferred to stone and cut by skilled craftsmen from the south.Composition, calligraphy and carving are together called the three perfections, and the collection is famous throughout the country.The residence was built in 1685, when Wang Yuyang enlarged the Western City Villa on the site of the Evergreen Garden laid out by his great-grandfather Wang Zhiyuan; it now covers fifteen thousand square metres with over seven thousand square metres of floor area and preserves one hundred and eight rooms of Ming, Qing and Republican date, the principal range five courtyards deep.Vast in scale, with carved beams and painted rafters, winding paths, dense woods and bamboo, it embodies a distinctive architectural style fusing official residence, vernacular dwelling, ancestral shrine and small garden, and is protected at province level.The Four Generations Palace Guard Arch was erected in 1619 to honour Wang Xiangqian, Wang Yuyang's great-uncle and Minister of War, who five times garrisoned the frontier and defended the state; the court posthumously granted the rank of Grand Master for Imperial Entertainments, Pillar of the State, Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of War to three preceding generations, whence the name Four Generations Palace Guard.The archway stands across the street facing south, fifteen metres high and 9.2 metres wide, in the palace form of a tall centre flanked by lower wings, the four large characters of its inscription written in a neat, powerful hand.It is the only one of the seventy-two archways of Xincheng to survive complete, and apart from its base is built entirely in carved brick, combining letters, architecture, sculpture, calligraphy and painting; original in form, imposing in presence and exquisite in workmanship, it is renowned for its archaic elegance and is called the first brick archway of China.

projects.name: 济南状元府与老城宅第群
projects.name_en: The Zhuangyuan Mansion and the Old-City Residences of Jinan
projects.level: 济南老城区内保存最好、等级最高的四合院之一
projects.address: 济南市历下区鞭指巷，省府前街以西、泉城路以北
projects.content_zh: 状元府位于济南老城区鞭指巷，是清咸丰年间济南历史上第二位状元陈冕的府第。陈冕（1859—1893年），字冠生，顺天宛平人，寄籍济南，光绪九年（1883年）中进士，殿试一甲第一名，钦点状元，授翰林院修撰。其祖父陈显彝于清咸丰年间在省府前街以西、泉城路以北的鞭指巷建造了这座府邸，是济南老城区内保存最好、等级最高、规模最大的四合院式建筑之一。状元府的建筑格局为多进四合院，坐北朝南，沿中轴线依次布置大门、二门、厅堂、正房、后楼，两侧配以厢房、耳房、书房、花园。建筑为抬梁式木构架、硬山顶、小青瓦屋面，屋脊两端做高翘的蝎子尾，门楼磨砖对缝、木雕精细，院内方砖铺地，正房前出廊，廊下施苏式彩画，整体风格庄重而不奢华，体现了科举世家「诗礼传家」的审美取向。状元府的价值不仅在于建筑本身，更在于它是济南老城科举文化与士绅社会的物质见证。济南自宋代以来即为山东的政治、文化中心，明清两代是济南府与历城县的治所，城内官署、书院、贡院、文庙林立，芙蓉街、鞭指巷、后宰门街、高都司巷一带是官宦与文人宅第的集中分布区，形成了独特的城市宅第文化区。济南老城的宅第群与泉水资源紧密结合，许多宅院内都有泉眼或引泉入院的渠道，泉水既供日常生活之用，又是园林造景的重要元素，形成了「泉—院—宅」三位一体的城市人居模式，这在中国北方城市中极为罕见，是济南作为国家历史文化名城最核心的价值所在。除状元府外，济南老城还保留了题壁堂、寿康楼等一批重要的公共与商业建筑。题壁堂建于清嘉庆八年（1803年），现保存三个院落，布局完整，是山东省现存规模最大的古代戏院之一，也是济南老城区内保存最为完整、基本保持始建原貌的一组古代公共商业建筑群；寿康楼由一座三层西式楼房与一座二层中式阁楼组成，据史料记载始建于清末，为当时《山东官报》的旧址，反映了近代中西建筑文化在济南的交汇。此外，济南老城还有翔凤巷这样的特色街巷，东起平泉胡同、西止芙蓉街，是济南最窄的小巷，宽度仅八十厘米，旧时为两边房子的墙缝形成，俗称「墙缝巷」，后取其谐音改称翔凤巷，寓意让凤凰飞到这里，图个吉祥；街中一间房的墙上嵌着清咸丰元年「翔凤巷」的刻石，是老城街巷文化的珍贵遗存。
projects.content_en: The Zhuangyuan, or Optimus, Mansion stands on Bianzhi Lane in the old city of Jinan and was the residence of Chen Mian, the second metropolitan optimus produced by Jinan, in the Xianfeng reign.Chen Mian (1859-1893), courtesy name Guansheng, came of a Wanping family registered in Jinan; he passed the metropolitan examination in 1883, placed first in the palace examination and was appointed a compiler in the Hanlin Academy.His grandfather Chen Xianyi built the mansion on Bianzhi Lane, west of the provincial government front street and north of Quancheng Road, during the Xianfeng era; it is one of the best-preserved, highest-ranking and largest courtyard houses in the old city of Jinan.The plan is a multi-courtyard siheyuan facing south, with gate, second gate, hall, principal rooms and rear building along the central axis, flanked by wings, ear rooms, a study and a garden.Construction is post-and-lintel timber framing with gable roofs and small grey tiles, the ridge ends turned up into scorpion tails, the gatehouse of rubbed brick with fine wood carving, the courtyards paved with square bricks, a veranda in front of the principal room and Suzhou-style polychrome painting beneath its eaves; the whole is dignified rather than ostentatious, expressing the aesthetic of an examination family that transmitted itself through poetry and ritual.The value of the mansion lies not only in the building itself but in its being the material witness of the examination culture and gentry society of old Jinan.A political and cultural centre of Shandong since the Song, Jinan was the seat of the prefecture and of Licheng county under the Ming and Qing, with government offices, academies, the examination hall and the Confucian temple within its walls; the area around Furong Street, Bianzhi Lane, Houzaimen Street and Gaodusi Lane held a concentration of official and literati residences, forming a distinctive urban mansion quarter.These residences are closely bound to the spring water: many courtyards contain their own spring or a channel leading in from one, the water serving daily needs and also functioning as an element of garden scenery, producing the three-in-one urban dwelling pattern of spring, courtyard, house - extremely rare among northern Chinese cities and the core value of Jinan as a national historical and cultural city.Besides the mansion, the old city preserves such important public and commercial buildings as the Tibi Hall and the Shoukang Building.The Tibi Hall, built in 1803, the eighth year of the Jiaqing reign, retains three complete courtyards and is one of the largest surviving ancient theatres in Shandong and the most intact group of ancient public commercial buildings in the old city, essentially in its original condition.The Shoukang Building consists of a three-storey western-style block and a two-storey Chinese pavilion; records date it to the late Qing, when it housed the Shandong Official Gazette, reflecting the meeting of Chinese and Western architectural culture in modern Jinan.The old city also preserves characteristic lanes such as Xiangfeng Lane, which runs east from Pingquan Alley to Furong Street and is the narrowest lane in Jinan at only eighty centimetres; originally formed as the gap between two houses and called the Wall-Crack Lane, it was renamed by homophone to Soaring Phoenix Lane for its auspicious meaning, and a stone dated to the first year of the Xianfeng reign set into a wall records the name - a precious survival of old-city lane culture.

projects.name: 胶东卫所与商人宅第群
projects.name_en: Garrison Towns and Merchant Residences of Jiaodong
projects.level: 中国历史文化名村／中国传统村落
projects.address: 烟台芝罘区所城里、蓬莱、莱州，威海荣成、文登，青岛即墨等
projects.content_zh: 胶东半岛是明清海防体系与近代商业文明交汇的地区，形成了两类特色鲜明的宅第群：一是以明代卫所制度为基础的军事性聚落宅第，二是以开埠通商为背景的商人宅第。明初为防御倭寇，朝廷在沿海设立卫所，山东境内设有登州卫、莱州卫、宁海卫、威海卫、成山卫、靖海卫、大嵩卫、鳌山卫等，形成「卫—所—寨—墩」的完整防御体系。卫所城池平面规整，呈方形或长方形，外围筑城墙、设城门、挖护城河，内部街巷呈棋盘格布局，十字大街将城内分为四区，民居按军事编制分配，规格统一、排列整齐，与普通农业村落自由生长的形态形成鲜明对比。烟台所城里是明代奇山守御千户所的城池，始建于明洪武三十一年（1398年），是中国现存最完整的明清海防卫所城池之一，城内的民居为典型的胶东四合院，青石墙基、青砖墙体、仰合瓦屋面，大门设在东南角，院内正房五间带前廊，经过近年来的保护性修缮，所城里已成为烟台最重要的历史文化街区。即墨雄崖所村是明代鳌山卫下辖的雄崖守御千户所城，位于青岛即墨区丰城镇海滨，始建于明洪武年间，因面对东北方白马岛上的雄伟断崖而得名，城堡呈正方形，边长各约五百米，城墙由夯土筑成外包青砖，设有奉恩门、镇威门两座城门与南西门，是中国现存最完整的明代海防所城之一，2008年被公布为中国历史文化名村。近代开埠之后，烟台、青岛相继成为通商口岸，商业繁荣催生了大批商人宅第。胶东商人宅第的特点是「中西合璧」：外观上保留胶东四合院的基本格局与硬山瓦顶，但在门楼、窗套、柱式、山花等处引入西方的拱券、线脚与装饰母题，室内则采用西式地板、壁炉、玻璃窗与石膏线脚，形成了独特的「中西合璧」风格，烟台朝阳街、广仁路一带的近代建筑群是其中的代表。龙口丁氏故宅、招远与莱州的商人宅院则是传统一脉的延续，其共同特点是布局严谨、用料考究、做工精细，以「黄县房」为代表，可与北京四合院相媲美，体现了胶东商人在财富积累之后对居住品质的追求，以及儒家伦理对商人宅第的深刻影响。
projects.content_en: The Jiaodong Peninsula is where the Ming and Qing coastal defence system met modern commercial civilisation, producing two sharply distinct groups of residences: the military settlements founded on the Ming garrison system, and the merchant houses that arose with the opening of the treaty ports.To guard against Japanese pirates, the early Ming court established guards and battalions along the coast; in Shandong these included Dengzhou, Laizhou, Ninghai, Weihai, Chengshan, Jinghai, Dasong and Aoshan guards, forming a complete defensive hierarchy of guard, battalion, fort and beacon.Garrison towns were laid out regularly on square or rectangular plans, walled with gates and moats, their internal streets on a grid divided into four quarters by a cross of main streets; dwellings were allotted according to military organisation with uniform standards and orderly arrangement, in sharp contrast to the free growth of ordinary farming villages.The Suochengli garrison town in Yantai, founded in 1398, was the walled town of the Qishan defence battalion and is among the most complete surviving Ming and Qing coastal garrison towns in China; its houses are typical Jiaodong courtyards with bluestone footings, grey brick walls and alternating concave-and-convex tiled roofs, the gate at the south-east corner and a five-bay principal room with front veranda within, and after conservation in recent years it has become the most important historical and cultural district in Yantai.Xiongyasuo Village in Jimo, the walled town of the Xiongya defence battalion under the Aoshan guard, lies on the coast at Fengcheng in Jimo District, Qingdao; founded in the Hongwu reign and named for the towering cliff facing Baima Island to the north-east, it is square, some five hundred metres on each side, with rammed-earth walls faced in grey brick, and gates known as Feng'en and Zhenwei together with south and west gates; it is one of the most complete surviving Ming coastal defence towns in China and was designated a China Historical and Cultural Village in 2008.With the opening of the ports in modern times, Yantai and Qingdao became treaty ports, and commercial prosperity produced a large number of merchant houses.Jiaodong merchant residences are characterised by a fusion of Chinese and Western: externally they keep the basic Jiaodong courtyard layout and gable tiled roof, but introduce Western arches, mouldings and decorative motifs at gatehouses, window surrounds, columns and gables, while interiors adopt Western floors, fireplaces, glazed windows and plaster cornices, producing a distinctive hybrid style represented by the modern buildings of Chaoyang Street and Guangren Road in Yantai.The Ding Family Residence in Longkou and the merchant houses of Zhaoyuan and Laizhou continue the traditional line; their common features are a rigorous layout, carefully chosen materials and fine workmanship, represented by the Huangxian house and comparable with the Beijing siheyuan, expressing both the pursuit of domestic quality that followed the accumulation of mercantile wealth and the profound influence of Confucian ethics on the merchant house.

projects.name: 山东庄园府第的防御体系与空间礼制
projects.name_en: Defensive Systems and Spatial Ritual in Shandong Manors
projects.address: 山东省全域
projects.content_zh: 山东庄园府第之所以在中国民居史上占有特殊地位，在于其同时具备两种看似矛盾的品质：一是极致的礼制秩序，二是完备的防御体系。前者源于山东作为儒家文化发源地的文化基因，后者则源于明清以来山东社会动荡、匪患频繁的历史现实，两者的结合塑造了山东庄园「外刚内柔、寓文于武」的独特品格。防御体系在山东庄园中呈现出由低到高的三个层级。第一层级是院落式防御，即依靠高大的院墙、厚重的门扇、多重院门的纵深设置来延缓入侵，这是最为普遍的做法，普通地主宅院即有之。院墙高度通常在三米以上，有的在墙头铺设瓦顶或插设碎瓷片防攀爬；大门用厚木板制作，内设门闩、顶门杠，门后设「更房」供值夜人居住。第二层级是城堡式防御，即在庄园外围构筑完整的城墙、护城河、吊桥、角楼、更道、垛口，形成一个独立的防御单元，惠民魏氏庄园是这一层级的巅峰之作，栖霞牟氏庄园亦属此类。第三层级是复合式防御，即在城堡式防御的基础上，于院内设置暗室、夹墙、地道、吊楼、悬楼等纵深防御设施，形成多点、多层、可退可守的立体防御网络，魏氏庄园的地道网与牟氏庄园的暗室夹墙都是典型实例。空间礼制则贯穿庄园府第的每一个层面。在整体布局上，中轴线是礼制秩序的脊梁，中路为尊，布置厅堂与祖堂，是祭祀、会客、议事的核心；东路为长，西路为宾，长幼尊卑各得其所。在建筑形制上，屋顶等级有严格区分：厅堂用悬山顶或歇山顶，正房用硬山顶，厢房、倒座、附属用房不得逾制；开间数量、举架高度、台基高度、彩画题材、脊兽数量，都与主人的社会地位严格对应。在行为规约上，庄园内的空间使用有明确的规范：女眷居于内宅，不得轻易外出，内外之间设「内门」「垂花门」加以分隔；「内言不出，外言不入」是基本的家法；佃户、长工、仆役只能在外院与附属院落活动，不得进入内宅；这些规约通过空间的分隔与门禁的设置得以固化，使建筑成为社会秩序的物质载体。值得注意的是，防御与礼制在山东庄园中并非彼此独立，而是互为表里：高大的院墙既是防御的屏障，也是内外有别的界限；多重的院门既是防御的纵深，也是礼仪的序列；重重院落既是防御的层次，也是长幼有序的等级。一座山东庄园，既是一座堡垒，也是一部礼书。这种「武备其外、文质其中」的双重性格，是理解山东庄园府第建筑的关键，也是齐鲁文化刚柔并济特质的建筑表达。
projects.content_en: The special place of Shandong manors in Chinese vernacular history rests on their possessing at once two seemingly contradictory qualities: an extreme ritual order on the one hand and a complete defensive system on the other.The first derives from Shandong's cultural genes as the birthplace of Confucianism, the second from the historical reality of social unrest and frequent banditry from the Ming and Qing onward; their combination produced the distinctive character of the Shandong manor as hard without and gentle within, the civil dwelling within the martial.Defence in Shandong manors appears at three ascending levels. The first is courtyard defence, relying on high walls, massive gates and the depth of successive gates to delay intrusion - the commonest method, found even in ordinary landlord houses.Walls usually exceed three metres, sometimes capped with tiles or set with broken porcelain to prevent climbing; gates are of thick planking with bars and props inside, and a watch room behind for the night guard.The second level is castle defence, in which a complete enceinte of wall, moat, drawbridge, corner towers, patrol walk and crenellations makes the manor an independent defensive unit; the Wei Family Manor in Huimin is the supreme example, and the Mou Family Manor in Qixia also belongs here.The third level is composite defence, which adds depth to the castle scheme by means of hidden rooms, double walls, tunnels, hung galleries and suspended galleries inside, forming a multi-point, multi-layer, three-dimensional defensive network allowing both resistance and withdrawal; the tunnel system of the Wei manor and the hidden rooms and double walls of the Mou manor are typical.Ritual order runs through every level of the manor. In overall layout the central axis is the spine of ritual order: the central route is honoured, holding the halls and ancestral shrine, the core of sacrifice, reception and deliberation; the eastern route belongs to the senior and the western to guests, so that old and young, honoured and humble, each has its place.In building form, roof rank is strictly graded: halls take hip-gable or overhanging gable roofs, principal rooms take gable roofs, and wings, reversal halls and ancillary buildings may not exceed their station; the number of bays, the height of the frame, the height of the platform, the subjects of polychrome painting and the number of ridge beasts all correspond exactly to the social rank of the owner.In conduct, the use of space within the manor is explicitly regulated: women live in the inner quarters and rarely go out, inner and outer being divided by an inner gate or a festooned gate; that inner words do not go out and outer words do not come in is a basic family rule; tenants, labourers and servants move only in the outer and service courts and may not enter the inner quarters.These rules are made permanent through spatial division and the placement of gates, making architecture the material vehicle of social order.It should be noted that defence and ritual in the Shandong manor are not independent but the outside and inside of the same thing: the high wall is at once a defensive barrier and the boundary between inner and outer; the successive gates are at once defensive depth and ceremonial sequence; the layered courtyards are at once defensive strata and the hierarchy of seniority.A Shandong manor is both a fortress and a book of rites, and this double character - martial provision without, civil substance within - is the key to understanding these buildings and the architectural expression of the Qilu cultural trait of combining hardness with gentleness.
highlights: 外刚内柔、寓文于武：山东庄园的双重品格

projects.name: 山东坛庙祠堂与礼制建筑概述
projects.name_en: An Overview of Altars, Temples, Ancestral Halls and Ritual Architecture in Shandong
projects.dynasty: 周代起源，汉唐发展，宋明清鼎盛
projects.address: 山东省全域，以曲阜、泰安、邹城、济南最为集中
projects.content_zh: 礼制建筑是中国古代建筑体系中等级最高、制度最严、延续最久的类型，其核心功能是通过建筑的空间秩序与形制等级来体现人神关系、君臣关系与宗法关系。山东作为儒家文化的发源地、齐鲁两大封国的故地、历代帝王封禅祭祀的所在，其礼制建筑的数量、等级与完整程度在全国首屈一指。山东的礼制建筑可以分为四大体系。第一是儒家祠庙体系，以曲阜孔庙为宗，下含颜庙（复圣庙）、曾庙（宗圣庙）、孟庙（亚圣庙）、周公庙（元圣庙）、尼山孔庙、以及各府州县的学宫文庙（如济南府学文庙），形成了自中央到地方的完整祭祀网络，是世界上延续时间最长、体系最完备的儒家祭祀建筑系统。第二是山川祭祀体系，以泰山岱庙与沂山东镇庙为代表，上承先秦「天子祭天下名山大川」的传统，下续秦汉以来帝王封禅与遣官致祭的制度，是全国唯一同时保存五岳之首（泰山）与五镇之首（沂山）祭祀建筑的省份。第三是家族宗祠体系，以孟府的家庙、新城王氏忠勤祠、丁氏故宅的堂号为代表，是宗法制度在乡土社会中的物质载体，凡是聚族而居的大姓村落，必设祠堂，形成「村必有祠、族必有谱」的格局。第四是民间信仰体系，包括妈祖（天后）庙、龙王庙、碧霞元君祠、关帝庙、土地庙等，这些建筑虽不属国家祀典，却是民众日常精神生活的中心。在建筑形制上，山东礼制建筑普遍遵循以下原则：一是中轴对称，沿南北纵轴依次布置照壁、棂星门（或戟门）、泮池、大成门（或仪门）、正殿、寝殿，层层递进，形成庄重的空间序列；二是等级分明，屋顶形式、开间数量、斗栱出跳、彩画题材、瓦色（黄琉璃、绿琉璃、灰筒瓦、灰板瓦）、脊兽数目，都与祭祀对象的等级严格对应；三是左庙右学或前庙后学，即将祭祀功能与教育功能结合，济南府学文庙「前庙后学」的格局即是典型；四是碑石林立，历代帝王的御制碑、文人的题咏碑、重修记事碑，构成了建筑群中独特的「石质档案」，曲阜孔庙与东镇庙的碑林都是全国闻名的碑刻宝库。山东礼制建筑的另一个重要价值在于其时代序列的完整性：从金元时期的尼山孔庙、颜庙，到明代的大成殿、奎文阁，再到清代的重修与增建，几乎各个朝代都有实物留存，构成了一部可以触摸的中国礼制建筑史。
projects.content_en: Ritual architecture is the highest-ranking, most strictly regulated and longest-enduring type in the Chinese architectural system; its essential function is to express through spatial order and graded form the relations between men and gods, ruler and subject, and the lineage itself.As the birthplace of Confucian culture, the home of the ancient states of Qi and Lu, and the site of imperial sacrifices through the ages, Shandong possesses ritual architecture unrivalled in the country in quantity, rank and completeness.Shandong ritual architecture falls into four systems. The first is the Confucian temple system, headed by the Confucius Temple at Qufu and comprising the Yan Temple of the Restored Sage, the Zeng Temple of the Ancestral Sage, the Mencius Temple of the Second Sage, the Duke of Zhou Temple of the Primordial Sage, the Nishan Confucius Temple, and the Confucian temples of prefectures, sub-prefectures and counties such as the Jinan Prefectural Confucian Temple - a complete sacrificial network from the centre to the localities and the longest-enduring, most complete system of Confucian sacrificial architecture in the world.The second is the mountain and river sacrificial system, represented by the Dai Temple at Mount Tai and the Eastern Peak Temple at Mount Yi; it continues the pre-Qin tradition that the Son of Heaven sacrifices to the famous mountains and great rivers of the realm and the later imperial practice of feng and shan sacrifices and of sending officials to offer sacrifice, and Shandong is the only province preserving the sacrificial architecture of both the first of the Five Great Mountains and the first of the Five Great Peaks.The third is the family ancestral hall system, represented by the family temple of the Mencius Mansion, the Zhongqin Hall of the Wang family of Xincheng and the hall names of the Ding Family Residence; it is the material vehicle of the lineage system in rural society, and wherever a great clan settled there had to be an ancestral hall, producing a pattern in which every village had its hall and every lineage its genealogy.The fourth is the system of popular belief, embracing temples of Mazu, the Dragon King, the Princess of the Azure Clouds, Lord Guan and the earth god; although outside the state sacrificial canon, these buildings were the centre of everyday spiritual life.In form, Shandong ritual architecture generally observes the following principles. First, axial symmetry: screen wall, Lattice Star Gate or halberd gate, pan pool, Dacheng or ceremonial gate, main hall and rear hall are laid out in sequence along a north-south axis, advancing layer by layer to form a solemn spatial progression.Second, clear gradation: roof form, number of bays, projection of dougong, subject of polychrome painting, tile colour - yellow glazed, green glazed, grey barrel or grey plate - and the number of ridge beasts all correspond strictly to the rank of the object of worship.Third, temple to the left and school to the right, or temple in front and school behind, combining sacrificial and educational functions; the temple in front, school behind arrangement of the Jinan Prefectural Confucian Temple is typical.Fourth, a forest of steles: imperial inscriptions, literary verses and records of rebuilding form a stone archive unique to these complexes, and the stele collections of the Confucius Temple at Qufu and of the Eastern Peak Temple are famous throughout the country.Another important value of Shandong ritual architecture is the completeness of its chronological sequence: from the Jin and Yuan structures of the Nishan Confucius Temple and the Yan Temple, through the Ming Dacheng Hall and Kuiwen Pavilion, to Qing rebuilding and additions, material from almost every dynasty survives, forming a history of Chinese ritual architecture that can be touched.
highlights: 山东礼制建筑数量等级完整程度全国首屈一指

projects.name: 曲阜孔庙
projects.name_en: The Confucius Temple in Qufu
projects.dynasty: 东周鲁哀公始立，历代重修，现存为明清格局
projects.level: 全国重点文物保护单位（1961年第一批）/ 世界文化遗产
projects.address: 济宁市曲阜市明故城内南门东侧
projects.content_zh: 曲阜孔庙是祭祀孔子的庙宇，位于曲阜明故城内，是中国现存规模最大、历史最悠久、保存最完整的孔庙，也是世界文化遗产「曲阜孔庙、孔林、孔府」的核心组成部分。孔庙的历史始于东周鲁哀公十七年（公元前478年），孔子去世后的第二年，鲁哀公将其故宅三间立为庙，'岁时奉祀'，此后历经两千四百余年的不断重修与扩建，形成今日占地约十四万平方米、九进院落、殿阁廊庑四百六十六间的宏大格局，其规模仅次于北京故宫，是中国三大宫殿式建筑群之一（另两处为北京故宫与承德避暑山庄）。孔庙的建筑沿南北中轴线展开，前后九进院落，前三进为引导性庭院，遍植桧柏，古木参天；自第四进起进入主体部分，依次为大中门、同文门、奎文阁、十三碑亭、大成门、杏坛、大成殿、寝殿、圣迹殿。奎文阁是孔庙的藏书楼，始建于北宋天禧二年（1018年），现存建筑为明弘治十三年（1500年）重建，面阔七间、进深五间，三层重檐歇山顶，高二十三米余，结构为独特的「层叠式」木构架——下层为木构架，上层为「暗层」，再上为顶层，内部采用「通柱」做法，即一根立柱贯通上下三层，是中国古代楼阁式藏书建筑中结构与功能结合的典范，历经数百年地震而完好无损。十三碑亭位于奎文阁与大成门之间，分列于道路两侧，共十三座，专为保存历代帝王御制石碑而建，其中有金、元碑亭各两座，清碑亭九座，碑亭均为重檐歇山顶，黄琉璃瓦覆顶，形制相近而年代各异，是研究历代建筑做法演变的重要实物。大成殿是孔庙的主体建筑，也是祭祀孔子的中心场所，面阔九间、进深五间，重檐歇山顶，覆黄色琉璃瓦，高约三十二米，与北京故宫太和殿、泰山岱庙天贶殿并称为中国三大宫殿式建筑。大殿最负盛名的是其檐下的十根深浮雕蟠龙石柱，每根柱上雕有双龙戏珠，龙身盘绕，鳞爪飞动，祥云缭绕，雕刻深达数厘米，层次丰富，立体感极强，据传每逢皇帝前来祭孔，都要用红布将石柱包裹，以免皇帝见此僭越之制而怪罪，足见其工艺之精绝。殿前有宽阔的月台，是祭孔时举行乐舞（八佾舞）的场所；殿内正中供奉孔子塑像，两侧为四配（颜回、曾参、孔伋、孟轲）与十二哲。杏坛位于大成殿之前，是孔子当年讲学之处，《庄子·渔父》载：孔子游乎缁帷之林，休坐乎杏坛之上，弟子读书，孔子弦歌鼓琴。现存杏坛为明隆庆三年（1569年）重建，重檐十字脊歇山顶，覆黄琉璃瓦，四面悬山，造型玲珑别致。孔庙内还保存有汉魏以来的历代碑刻一千余通，包括汉《乙瑛碑》《礼器碑》《史晨碑》等名碑，被誉为中国第二碑林，是研究中国古代政治、文化、书法艺术的宝库。
projects.content_en: The Confucius Temple in Qufu, standing inside the Ming walled city, is the largest, oldest and best-preserved Confucian temple in China and the core of the World Heritage site Temple and Cemetery of Confucius and the Kong Family Mansion.Its history begins in 478 BC, the year after Confucius died, when Duke Ai of Lu set up his three-room former residence as a temple for seasonal sacrifice; over more than two thousand four hundred years of continuous rebuilding and enlargement it has reached its present scale of some fourteen hectares, nine successive courtyards and four hundred and sixty-six halls, pavilions and corridors - second in size only to the Beijing Forbidden City and one of the three great palace-style complexes of China, the others being the Forbidden City and the Chengde Mountain Resort.The temple is laid out along a north-south axis in nine courts: the first three are introductory, planted with juniper and cypress whose ancient canopies soar; from the fourth begins the main body, with the Dazhong Gate, the Tongwen Gate, the Kuiwen Pavilion, the thirteen stele pavilions, the Dacheng Gate, the Apricot Terrace, the Dacheng Hall, the Rear Hall and the Hall of Sacred Traces.The Kuiwen Pavilion, the temple library, was first built in 1018 and the present structure dates from the rebuilding of 1500; seven bays wide and five deep, with three storeys under a double-eave hip-gable roof and a height of over twenty-three metres, it uses a distinctive stacked construction - a timber frame below, a hidden storey above and a top storey over that - with through-columns running the full three storeys, making it a model of the union of structure and function among Chinese library towers; it has survived centuries of earthquakes intact.The thirteen stele pavilions, ranged on both sides of the way between the Kuiwen Pavilion and the Dacheng Gate, were built expressly to house imperial steles: two from the Jin, two from the Yuan and nine from the Qing, all with double-eave hip-gable roofs and yellow glazed tiles; similar in form but different in date, they are important material for studying the evolution of building practice.The Dacheng Hall is the main building and the centre of the sacrifice to Confucius: nine bays wide and five deep, with a double-eave hip-gable roof in yellow glazed tiles and a height of about thirty-two metres, it is counted with the Hall of Supreme Harmony in the Forbidden City and the Tiankuang Hall of the Dai Temple at Mount Tai as one of the three great palace halls of China.Its most famous feature is the ten deep-relief coiled dragon stone columns under its eaves, each carved with two dragons playing with a pearl, their bodies coiling, scales and claws in motion, amid encircling clouds; the relief is several centimetres deep, richly layered and powerfully three-dimensional.Tradition holds that whenever an emperor came to sacrifice, the columns were wrapped in red cloth lest he take offence at so transgressive a display - a sufficient testimony to their extraordinary craftsmanship.In front of the hall a broad moon terrace served for the eight-row dance performed at the sacrifice; inside, the central image of Confucius is flanked by the four correlates - Yan Hui, Zeng Can, Kong Ji and Mencius - and the twelve philosophers.The Apricot Terrace in front of the hall marks the place where Confucius taught; the Zhuangzi records that Confucius wandered in the forest of Ziwei and rested above the Apricot Terrace, his disciples reading while he sang to the strings.The present structure was rebuilt in 1569, with a double-eave cross-ridge hip-gable roof in yellow glazed tiles and overhanging gables on four sides, exquisite and unusual in form.The temple also preserves more than a thousand steles from the Han and Wei onward, including famous ones such as the Yiying, Liqi and Shichen steles of the Han, and is honoured as the second forest of steles in China, a treasury for the study of Chinese politics, culture and calligraphy.
highlights: 东周鲁哀公十七年（前478）立庙，两千四百余年延续
占地约十四万平方米，九进院落，殿阁廊庑四百六十六间
中国三大宫殿式建筑群之一，仅次于北京故宫
奎文阁三层重檐歇山，通柱做法，历经地震无损
十三碑亭：金元各二座、清九座，黄琉璃重檐歇山
大成殿九间重檐歇山黄琉璃，与太和殿、天贶殿并称
十根深浮雕蟠龙石柱，皇帝亲祭须以红布包裹
汉魏以来碑刻一千余通，中国第二碑林

projects.name: 泰山岱庙
projects.name_en: The Dai Temple at Mount Tai
projects.dynasty: 汉代始建，宋金元明清历代重修
projects.level: 全国重点文物保护单位（1988年第三批）/ 世界文化遗产
projects.address: 泰安市泰山区，泰山南麓泰安城内
projects.content_zh: 岱庙又称东岳庙，是历代帝王祭祀泰山神的庙宇，位于泰山南麓的泰安城内，是泰山古建筑群的核心，也是泰山世界文化与自然遗产的重要组成部分。岱庙的历史可以追溯到汉代，据《宋天贶殿碑铭》记载：秦既作畴，汉亦起宫——汉武帝时期曾在泰山下建「泰山宫」，其后历代增修，至北宋大中祥符年间（1008—1016年）宋真宗封禅泰山，大兴土木扩建岱庙，奠定了今日的基本格局。岱庙占地约九万六千平方米，平面呈长方形，四周筑有城墙，周长约一点五公里，设有八个城门，是名副其实的城中之城；城墙上建有角楼、门楼，城外有护城河环绕，这种「庙城合一」的形制在中国祠庙建筑中极为罕见，体现了泰山神作为「五岳之首」的崇高地位。岱庙的建筑沿南北中轴线展开，自南向北依次为遥参亭、岱庙坊、正阳门、配天门、仁安门、天贶殿、后寝宫、厚载门，东路为汉柏院、东御座，西路为唐槐院、雨花道院，形成了「中轴为主、两翼为辅」的完整格局。天贶殿是岱庙的主体建筑，也是泰山神府的正殿，面阔九间、进深四间，重檐庑殿顶，覆黄色琉璃瓦，高二十二米余，与北京故宫太和殿、曲阜孔庙大成殿并称为中国三大宫殿式建筑。殿内供奉东岳泰山神像，最为珍贵的是殿内北、东、西三面墙上的巨幅壁画《泰山神启跸回銮图》，全长六十二米，高三点三米，以泰山神出巡与回銮为题材，绘有六百九十余个神态各异的人物，以及形态生动的山石树木、宫殿桥涵与祥禽瑞兽，场面宏大、构图严谨、笔法流畅、色彩典雅，是中国现存最大、最完整的古代壁画之一，据考为宋代创作、明清重摹，是研究宋代绘画与古代卤簿仪仗制度的珍贵实物。岱庙内还有极为著名的汉柏与唐槐。汉柏院中有五株相传为汉武帝亲手所植的柏树，历经两千余年仍然苍劲挺拔，树干扭曲盘旋，树皮纹理如龙鳞，被誉为「活的文物」，是泰山「古、奇、拙、朴」精神的象征。唐槐院中的唐槐相传为唐代所植，虽主干已空，但新枝繁茂，形成「槐中抱子」的奇观。岱庙内还保存有历代碑刻一百五十余通，其中最著名的是秦代李斯小篆《泰山刻石》（仅存九字残石，移置岱庙）、汉代《张迁碑》《衡方碑》、晋代《孙夫人碑》、唐代《纪泰山铭》（摩崖刻石，在岱顶大观峰）的宋代摹刻本等，是中国书法艺术的宝库。此外，岱庙的铜亭（明万历四十三年铜铸，原在岱顶碧霞祠，后移置岱庙）、铁塔（明嘉靖年间铸铁塔，现存三层）也都是珍贵的文物。
projects.content_en: The Dai Temple, also called the Eastern Peak Temple, is where successive emperors sacrificed to the god of Mount Tai; it stands in the city of Tai'an at the southern foot of the mountain, is the core of the Mount Tai ancient building complex and an important part of the Mount Tai World Cultural and Natural Heritage site.Its history reaches back to the Han: according to the Song inscription recording the Tiankuang Hall, the Qin built altars and the Han raised palaces, and the Han emperor Wudi built a Mount Tai palace at the foot of the mountain, which later dynasties enlarged; in the Dazhongxiangfu era of the Song (1008-1016), when the emperor Zhenzong performed the feng and shan sacrifices at Mount Tai, he had the temple greatly extended, establishing the basic plan seen today.The temple covers some ninety-six thousand square metres on a rectangular plan, enclosed by a wall about one and a half kilometres in circumference with eight gates - in effect a city within a city; corner and gate towers rise on the wall and a moat encircles it, a fusion of temple and city almost unknown among Chinese temple complexes and an expression of the supreme rank of the god of Mount Tai as first of the Five Great Mountains.Its buildings run along a north-south axis: from the south, the Yaocan Pavilion, the Dai Temple archway, the Zhengyang Gate, the Peitian Gate, the Ren'an Gate, the Tiankuang Hall, the Rear Resting Palace and the Houzai Gate, with the Han Cypress Court and the Eastern Imperial Seat to the east and the Tang Locust Court and the Yuhua Taoist Court to the west, forming a complete scheme of a dominant central axis with subordinate wings.The Tiankuang Hall is the main building and the principal hall of the god's residence: nine bays wide and four deep, with a double-eave hip roof in yellow glazed tiles and a height of over twenty-two metres; it is counted with the Hall of Supreme Harmony in the Forbidden City and the Dacheng Hall of the Confucius Temple at Qufu as one of the three great palace halls of China.It enshrines the image of the god of Mount Tai, but its greatest treasure is the enormous mural on the north, east and west walls, the Departure and Return of the God of Mount Tai, sixty-two metres long and 3.3 metres high, depicting the god's procession out and his return, with more than 690 figures of varied expression, vivid rocks and trees, palaces and bridges, and auspicious birds and beasts.Grand in scale, rigorous in composition, fluent in brushwork and elegant in colour, it is one of the largest and most complete surviving ancient murals in China, thought to have been created in the Song and retraced in the Ming and Qing, and is precious material for the study of Song painting and of ancient ceremonial procession.The temple is also famous for its Han cypresses and Tang locust.In the Han Cypress Court five trees said to have been planted by the Han emperor Wudi himself still stand vigorous after more than two thousand years, their trunks twisted and coiling and their bark scaled like a dragon, honoured as living monuments and embodying the spirit of Mount Tai as ancient, strange, unhewn and plain.The Tang locust in the Tang Locust Court, said to date from the Tang, has a hollow trunk yet flourishes with new branches, producing the marvel of a child held within the locust.The temple also preserves more than one hundred and fifty steles, among them the Qin seal-script Mount Tai inscription of Li Si, of which only a nine-character fragment survives, moved here for safekeeping; the Han steles of Zhang Qian and Heng Fang; the Jin stele of Lady Sun; and a Song tracing of the Tang Record of the Sacrifice at Mount Tai, originally cut on the cliff at Daguan Peak - a treasury of Chinese calligraphy.In addition, the bronze pavilion cast in 1615 and originally at the Azure Cloud Temple on the summit, and the iron pagoda of the Jiajing reign, of which three storeys survive, are both precious artefacts.

projects.name: 泰山碧霞祠与泰山古建筑群
projects.name_en: The Bixia Temple and the Ancient Building Complex of Mount Tai
projects.level: 全国重点文物保护单位 / 世界文化与自然双重遗产
projects.address: 泰安市泰山主峰南麓天街东首
projects.content_zh: 碧霞祠位于泰山天街东首、玉皇顶南麓，是祭祀泰山女神「碧霞元君」的庙宇，是泰山古建筑群中位置最高、规模最大的一组高山建筑，也是中国高山建筑的杰出代表。碧霞元君全称为「东岳泰山天仙玉女碧霞元君」，民间俗称「泰山老奶奶」「泰山娘娘」，是华北地区最具影响力的女神之一，其信仰自宋代兴起，明清两代达到鼎盛，形成了「南妈祖、北碧霞」的民间信仰格局。碧霞祠始建于北宋大中祥符年间（1008—1016年），宋真宗封禅泰山时在岱顶发现玉女石像，遂建「昭真祠」供奉，金代改称「昭真观」，明代改称「碧霞灵应宫」，清代定名为「碧霞祠」，现存建筑为明清两代重修的遗构。碧霞祠的建筑布局依山就势，坐北朝南，前有山门、钟鼓楼，中为香亭，后为正殿，正殿面阔五间、进深三间，重檐歇山顶，覆铁瓦（正殿）与铜瓦（配殿），这种以金属为瓦的做法是中国高山建筑的独特创造：泰山极顶海拔一千五百余米，风力强劲、气温极低，普通陶瓦易被狂风掀翻、被冰冻酥裂，而铁瓦与铜瓦重量大、强度高、抗风抗冻性能优异，虽然造价高昂，却能确保建筑在极端气候条件下长久保存，是古代匠师针对高山环境做出的理性选择。正殿内供奉碧霞元君铜像，殿前有明代铸造的千斤铜鼎与铜亭，香火极盛，每逢农历三月十五日碧霞元君诞辰，前来进香的善男信女络绎不绝。碧霞祠的价值不仅在于建筑本身，更在于它是泰山古建筑群的代表。泰山古建筑群沿登山轴线分布，自岱宗坊起，经红门宫、万仙楼、斗母宫、中天门、云步桥、五大夫松、朝阳洞、对松山、十八盘、南天门、天街，直至碧霞祠、玉皇顶、日观峰，形成了一条绵延十余公里、高差一千三百余米的立体建筑序列，各类建筑依山就势、因地制宜，与山体、植被、岩石融为一体，体现了「建筑与自然共生」的最高境界，是世界文化与自然双重遗产的核心价值所在。在这一序列中，还有一类特殊的建筑形式——摩崖石刻。泰山摩崖石刻现存一千余处，其中最著名的是唐玄宗李隆基撰书的《纪泰山铭》，刻于岱顶大观峰崖壁，高十三点三米、宽五点三米，共九百九十六字，字体为唐隶，遒劲雄浑，是唐代隶书的代表作，也是中国现存最大的摩崖石刻之一。这些摩崖石刻与古建筑、古遗址共同构成了泰山作为「露天书法博物馆」的独特地位。
projects.content_en: The Bixia Temple stands at the eastern end of the Heavenly Street on the southern slope below the Jade Emperor Peak; it is the temple of the goddess of Mount Tai, the Princess of the Azure Clouds, and is the highest and largest group of high-mountain buildings in the Mount Tai complex, as well as an outstanding representative of Chinese mountain architecture.The goddess's full title is the Jade Maiden of the Azure Clouds, Immortal of Heaven, of the Eastern Peak Mount Tai; popularly known as the Old Grandmother of Mount Tai or the Lady of Mount Tai, she is among the most influential female deities of north China.Her cult arose in the Song and reached its height in the Ming and Qing, producing the popular pattern of Mazu in the south and the Azure Clouds in the north.The temple was founded in the Dazhongxiangfu era of the Northern Song (1008-1016): when the emperor Zhenzong performed the feng and shan sacrifices he found a stone image of a jade maiden on the summit and built the Shining Truth Shrine to house it; it was renamed Shining Truth Abbey under the Jin, Palace of the Responsive Azure Clouds under the Ming, and finally Bixia Temple under the Qing; the surviving buildings are the work of Ming and Qing rebuilding.The layout follows the mountain, facing south: a mountain gate and bell and drum towers in front, an incense pavilion in the middle and the main hall behind; the hall is five bays wide and three deep with a double-eave hip-gable roof, covered in iron tiles on the main hall and bronze tiles on the flanking halls.This use of metal for roof tiles is a distinctive invention of Chinese high-mountain architecture: the summit of Mount Tai lies at over fifteen hundred metres, with violent winds and very low temperatures, and ordinary ceramic tiles are easily torn off by gales or cracked by frost, whereas iron and bronze tiles are heavy, strong and resistant to wind and freezing; costly though they are, they ensure the survival of the building under extreme conditions, a rational choice made by ancient builders in response to the mountain environment.The hall enshrines a bronze image of the goddess, and before it stand a thousand-catty bronze ding and a bronze pavilion cast in the Ming; incense burns ceaselessly, and on the fifteenth day of the third lunar month, the goddess's birthday, pilgrims come in an unending stream.The value of the temple lies not only in the building itself but in its being representative of the whole Mount Tai complex.That complex is distributed along the climbing axis, from the Daizong Archway through the Red Gate Palace, the Tower of Ten Thousand Immortals, the Doumu Palace, the Middle Gate of Heaven, the Cloud-Step Bridge, the Five Great Officers Pine, the Sun-Facing Cave, the Opposing Pines Mountain, the Eighteen Turns, the South Gate of Heaven and the Heavenly Street to the Bixia Temple, the Jade Emperor Peak and the Sun-Viewing Peak, forming a three-dimensional architectural sequence more than ten kilometres long with a rise of over thirteen hundred metres.Following the mountain and adapting to local conditions, these buildings merge with the massif, the vegetation and the rock, embodying the highest ideal of architecture living in symbiosis with nature, which is the core value of the World Cultural and Natural Heritage site.Within this sequence there is also a special building form, the cliff inscription; more than a thousand survive on Mount Tai, the most famous being the Record of the Sacrifice at Mount Tai composed and written by the Tang emperor Xuanzong, cut on the cliff face at Daguan Peak near the summit, 13.3 metres high and 5.3 metres wide, in 996 characters of Tang clerical script, vigorous and majestic - a representative work of Tang clerical calligraphy and one of the largest surviving cliff inscriptions in China.Together with the buildings and the ancient sites, these inscriptions give Mount Tai its unique standing as an open-air museum of calligraphy.

projects.name: 曲阜颜庙与尼山孔庙及书院
projects.name_en: The Yan Temple and the Nishan Confucius Temple and Academy in Qufu
projects.dynasty: 颜庙元代始建，尼山孔庙金代重建
projects.level: 全国重点文物保护单位（2001年第五批、2006年第六批）
projects.address: 济宁市曲阜市鼓楼北街4号（颜庙）、曲阜市尼山镇（尼山孔庙）
projects.content_zh: 颜庙又称复圣庙，位于曲阜城北门内陋巷街北首，与孔府后花园隔街相望，是祭祀孔子最得意的弟子颜回的庙宇。颜回字子渊，是孔子弟子中德行最高的一位，《论语》中记载：一箪食，一瓢饮，在陋巷，人不堪其忧，回也不改其乐；唐太宗尊之为「先师」，唐玄宗尊之为「兖公」，宋真宗加封为「兖国公」，元文宗尊为「兖国复圣公」，明嘉靖九年改称「复圣」。颜庙规模宏大，占地三十六亩，地基南边宽、北边窄，呈不规则形状，整体为三路布局、五进院落，有殿、亭、门、坊等建筑一百五十余间，古树五百余株，正殿为复圣殿，供奉颜回塑像，西边奉祀颜回之父颜路。颜庙的建筑完整地体现了元、明、清三代的建筑特色，并保存有金代至清代的碑刻文献，是研究元明时期建筑做法的重要实例，2001年被国务院公布为第五批全国重点文物保护单位。尼山孔庙及书院位于曲阜城东南约三十公里的尼山，尼山是孔子的诞生地，原名尼丘山，因避孔子名丘之讳而改称尼山。尼山孔庙始建于五代后周显德年间（954—960年），宋庆历三年（1043年）孔子四十六代孙孔宗愿扩建，金明昌五年（1194年）大修，元至元四年（1267年）、明永乐十五年（1417年）等多次重修，现存建筑主要为金元时期的遗构，2006年被国务院公布为第六批全国重点文物保护单位。尼山孔庙依山而建，坐北朝南，由庙宇与书院两部分组成：庙宇部分自南向北依次为棂星门、观川亭、大成门、大成殿、寝殿，大成殿面阔五间，单檐歇山顶，覆绿琉璃瓦，殿内供奉孔子及四配塑像；书院部分位于庙宇东北，为讲学之所，有大门、正房、东西厢房等，是研究中国古代书院建筑与教育制度的重要实例。尼山还有著名的夫子洞（坤灵洞），相传为孔子出生之处，洞内有孔子及其母颜徵在的石像；观川亭位于庙宇东南角的崖畔，相传孔子曾在此观五川汇流，《论语》中有「子在川上曰：逝者如斯夫，不舍昼夜」的名句，即出自此处。颜庙与尼山孔庙的价值在于它们与孔庙共同构成了完整的儒家祭祀体系：孔庙为「至圣」，颜庙为「复圣」，曾庙为「宗圣」，孟庙为「亚圣」，四庙并立，共同体现了儒家「道统」传承的建筑表达，这在世界宗教建筑史上是极为罕见的完整体系。
projects.content_en: The Yan Temple, also called the Temple of the Restored Sage, stands at the northern end of Louxiang Street inside the north gate of Qufu, facing the rear garden of the Confucius Mansion across the street; it is the temple of Yan Hui, the most accomplished of Confucius's disciples.Yan Hui, courtesy name Ziyuan, ranked first among the disciples in virtue; the Analects record that with a single bamboo dish of rice and a single gourd of water in a mean alley, where others could not bear the hardship, he did not change his joy.The Tang emperor Taizong honoured him as First Teacher, Xuanzong as Duke of Yan, the Song emperor Zhenzong as Duke of the State of Yan, the Yuan emperor Wenzong as Duke of the State of Yan, Restored Sage, and in 1530 the title was changed to Restored Sage.The temple is large, occupying thirty-six mu on an irregular site broad to the south and narrow to the north, in three routes and five courtyards with more than one hundred and fifty halls, pavilions, gates and archways and over five hundred ancient trees; the principal hall, the Hall of the Restored Sage, enshrines an image of Yan Hui, and to its west is honoured his father Yan Lu.The buildings fully express the architectural character of the Yuan, Ming and Qing and preserve inscriptions from the Jin to the Qing, making the temple an important example for the study of Yuan and Ming building practice; it was listed by the State Council in 2001 in the fifth batch of National Key Cultural Heritage Sites.The Nishan Confucius Temple and Academy lie on Mount Ni, some thirty kilometres south-east of Qufu, the birthplace of Confucius; the mountain was originally Mount Niqiu, renamed Mount Ni to avoid the taboo on Confucius's personal name Qiu.The temple was founded in the Xiande era of the Later Zhou (954-960), extended in 1043 by Kong Zongyuan, a descendant of Confucius in the forty-sixth generation, greatly repaired in 1194, and rebuilt many times thereafter, in 1267, 1417 and later; the surviving buildings are essentially of Jin and Yuan date, and the site was listed by the State Council in 2006 in the sixth batch.The complex is built against the mountain facing south and consists of temple and academy.The temple runs from south to north through the Lattice Star Gate, the River-Viewing Pavilion, the Dacheng Gate, the Dacheng Hall and the Rear Hall; the Dacheng Hall is five bays wide with a single-eave hip-gable roof in green glazed tiles and enshrines Confucius and the four correlates.The academy lies to the north-east of the temple and was the place of teaching, with a gate, principal rooms and east and west wings; it is an important example for the study of Chinese academy architecture and the educational system.Mount Ni also has the famous Master's Cave, or Kunling Cave, where Confucius is said to have been born, containing stone images of Confucius and his mother Yan Zhengzai; and the River-Viewing Pavilion stands on the cliff at the south-east corner of the temple, where Confucius is said to have watched the confluence of five streams, the occasion of the famous saying in the Analects, The Master stood by a stream and said: thus does it flow on, never ceasing day or night.The value of the Yan Temple and the Nishan temple lies in their completing, with the Confucius Temple, the whole Confucian sacrificial system: the Confucius Temple for the Ultimate Sage, the Yan Temple for the Restored Sage, the Zeng Temple for the Ancestral Sage and the Mencius Temple for the Second Sage - four temples standing together as the architectural expression of the transmission of the Confucian Way, a completeness rare in the history of religious architecture anywhere.

projects.name: 嘉祥曾庙与曲阜周公庙
projects.name_en: The Zeng Temple in Jiaxiang and the Duke of Zhou Temple in Qufu
projects.dynasty: 曾庙明代，周公庙宋大中祥符元年（1008）始建
projects.level: 全国重点文物保护单位（曾庙2006年第六批、周公庙2013年第七批）
projects.address: 济宁市嘉祥县满硐镇南武山村（曾庙）、曲阜市鲁城街道（周公庙）
projects.content_zh: 曾庙又称宗圣庙，位于济宁市嘉祥县满硐镇南武山村西，是祭祀曾子的专庙。曾子名参，字子舆，春秋末年鲁国南武城（今嘉祥）人，与其父曾点同为孔子弟子，比孔子小四十六岁，是孔子弟子中年纪较轻而造诣甚高的一位，被后世尊奉为「宗圣」。《论语》中记载曾子「吾日三省吾身」的名言，相传《大学》《孝经》皆出其手，是儒家「修齐治平」思想的重要传承者。曾庙为古代官式建筑群体，明代建筑风格，建筑布局沿中轴线分正、左、右三路，共五进院落，庙内碑碣林立，古柏参天，更显肃穆壮观，2006年被国务院公布为第六批全国重点文物保护单位。曲阜周公庙全称文宪王庙，亦称元圣庙，是祭祀周公姬旦的庙宇，位于曲阜市鲁城街道。周公姓姬名旦，是周文王的第四子、武王的弟弟，辅佐武王伐纣建立周朝，并制定了典章制度（即「制礼作乐」）；按周朝宗法制度，周公被分封于鲁，因周公留佐成王，故由其长子伯禽就封建鲁国；因周公佐周之功，特许伯禽于鲁设立太庙以祀远祖，周公死后并祀之。宋真宗大中祥符元年（1008年），周公被追封为「文宪王」，并在鲁太庙的旧址上为周公建庙。周公庙历经宋、元、明、清六次修建，占地两万八千平方米，三进院落，有门、坊、亭、殿等明清建筑十三座五十七间，尚有碑刻三十五通及桧、柏等古树名木。庙院坐北朝南，三进院落布局，现存建筑包括棂星门、「经天纬地」石坊、「制礼作乐」石坊、承德门、达孝门、御碑亭、元圣殿、东庑、西庑等。棂星门为三间四柱三楼冲天柱式，门内东西两侧立「经天纬地」石坊与「制礼作乐」石坊，两坊均为明嘉靖三年（1524年）冬十月由山东巡抚都察院右副都御史陈凤梧等建立，石质四楹三间，中额刻字，两次间均浅刻二龙戏珠图案，以赞颂周公的历史功绩。元圣殿是周公庙的中心建筑，面阔五间二十三点七米，进深三间十二点二六米，通高十一点八一米，单檐歇山绿琉璃瓦顶，重昂五踩斗栱，殿内塑有周公像，正中上悬「明德勤施」匾额，殿前有露台，两侧有形制相同的东西庑。院中置有明代雕刻的盘龙石香炉一座，两旁立有宋元明清的石碑十六幢，其中西边中间的一幢是周公庙现存最早的御碑，为宋真宗大中祥符元年由真宗撰书的《文宪王赞碑》。2013年5月，曲阜周公庙入选第七批全国重点文物保护单位。曾庙与周公庙的价值在于它们共同体现了鲁国故地的礼制传统：周公是周礼的制定者，曾子是儒家道统的传承者，二者一为礼之源、一为礼之承，与孔庙共同构成了曲阜「礼制建筑群」的完整谱系。
projects.content_en: The Zeng Temple, also called the Temple of the Ancestral Sage, lies west of Nanwushan Village in Manjiong Township, Jiaxiang County, Jining, and is the temple dedicated to Zengzi.Zengzi, given name Can, courtesy name Ziyu, was a native of Nanwucheng in the state of Lu - today's Jiaxiang - in the late Spring and Autumn period; he and his father Zeng Dian were both disciples of Confucius, and although forty-six years younger than the Master he was among the most accomplished of them, honoured by later ages as the Ancestral Sage.The Analects record his famous saying that he examines himself three times a day, and the Great Learning and the Classic of Filial Piety are traditionally ascribed to him, making him a key transmitter of the Confucian programme of self-cultivation, family order, statecraft and peace.The temple is an official-style complex of Ming character, laid out along a central axis in main, left and right routes with five successive courtyards; steles crowd the precinct and ancient cypresses tower above it, giving an air of solemn grandeur, and it was listed by the State Council in 2006 in the sixth batch of National Key Cultural Heritage Sites.The Duke of Zhou Temple in Qufu, fully the Temple of the King of Culture and Constitution, also called the Temple of the Primordial Sage, is the temple of Ji Dan, the Duke of Zhou, and stands in Lucheng Subdistrict.The Duke of Zhou, of the Ji clan and named Dan, was the fourth son of King Wen and brother of King Wu; he helped overthrow the Shang and found the Zhou, and established its institutions - the making of ritual and music.By the Zhou law of succession he was enfeoffed at Lu, but because he remained to assist King Cheng his eldest son Boqin went in his place and founded the state of Lu; in recognition of his service to the Zhou, Boqin was permitted to establish a grand temple at Lu to sacrifice to remote ancestors, and after his death the Duke of Zhou was jointly worshipped there.In 1008 the Song emperor Zhenzong posthumously enfeoffed him as King of Culture and Constitution and built a temple on the site of the old grand temple of Lu.Rebuilt six times under the Song, Yuan, Ming and Qing, the temple covers twenty-eight thousand square metres in three courtyards with thirteen Ming and Qing structures - gates, archways, pavilions and halls - comprising fifty-seven bays, together with thirty-five steles and ancient junipers and cypresses.It faces south in three courts, and the surviving buildings are the Lattice Star Gate, the stone archways of Ordering Heaven and Earth and of Ritual and Music, the Chengde Gate, the Daxiao Gate, the Imperial Stele Pavilion, the Hall of the Primordial Sage and the east and west corridors.The Lattice Star Gate has three bays, four columns and three tiers in the soaring-column manner; inside it stand the two stone archways, both erected in October 1524 by Chen Fengwu, right vice censor-in-chief and touring governor of Shandong; each is of stone with four pillars and three bays, the central tablet inscribed and the flanking bays carved in shallow relief with two dragons playing with a pearl, celebrating the Duke's historical achievement.The Hall of the Primordial Sage is the central building: five bays or 23.7 metres wide, three bays or 12.26 metres deep, and 11.81 metres high, with a single-eave hip-gable roof in green glazed tiles and double-ang five-step dougong.It houses an image of the Duke of Zhou and hangs a plaque, Virtue Made Bright and Diligent in Deeds; before it is a terrace flanked by identical east and west corridors.In the court stands a Ming carved stone incense burner with coiled dragons, and on either side are sixteen steles of the Song, Yuan, Ming and Qing; the central one on the west is the oldest imperial stele in the temple, the Hymn to the King of Culture and Constitution, composed and written by the emperor Zhenzong in 1008.In May 2013 the temple was added to the seventh batch of National Key Cultural Heritage Sites.The value of the Zeng and Duke of Zhou temples lies in their expressing together the ritual tradition of the old state of Lu: the Duke of Zhou was the author of the Zhou rites and Zengzi the transmitter of the Confucian Way - one the source of ritual, the other its continuation - and with the Confucius Temple they form a complete genealogy of the ritual architecture of Qufu.
